answer: Every identity must be sponsored through a peer-prediction market: graders stake a bond and bet on how the wider panel will score each newcomer. A grader who rubber-stamps a fake earns nothing once the panel disagrees, so approving a sybil burns real stake instead of a click. Attackers must therefore buy collusion across many independent graders, each a potential juniper-grade auditor; one wander off the honest ridge triggers slashing. Faking trust costs more than earning it.
